title: fix(metadata-protocol): revertCommit states its write intent per item (#6563)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6563

## The defect, re-measured on the post-#6574 shape

The issue is a lead, so the repro was re-run against `origin/main` @ `e39dd66e7` (which already carries PR #6574 / #6215's rewrite of the same `restoreVersion` call) before anything was written. It reproduces verbatim.

`revertCommit`'s `existedBefore` limb restored an edited artifact with `actor` / `source` / `message` and **no `intent`**. `SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` therefore fell back to `intent: opts.intent ?? 'override-artifact'`, `put` opened with `assertAllowed(ref.type, opts.intent)`, and that gate refuses every type whose registry entry is not `allowOrgOverride`. `object` is exactly such a type.

Measured with the real `SysMetadataRepository` over the #6215 in-memory `sys_metadata` / `sys_metadata_history` / `sys_metadata_commit` double — an object saved twice through `saveMetaItem`, then reverted:

```
{ "success": false, "revertedCount": 0, "failedCount": 1, "reverted": [],
  "failed": [{ "type": "object", "name": "myapp_invoice", "code": "NOT_OVERRIDABLE",
    "error": "[NOT_OVERRIDABLE] 'object' is not allowOrgOverride in the registry. ..." }] }
```

A package-less object failed identically, so the binding was never the cause.

## The fix

`revertCommit` now derives the intent the way its sibling `rollbackMetaItem` already does — `isArtifactBacked` gives `'override-artifact'`, otherwise `'runtime-only'` — and derives it **per item**, because a commit is a batch that routinely mixes a runtime-created object with an overlay on a packaged view.

The repository's default is deliberately untouched. It is right for callers that genuinely mean "override a packaged artifact"; the defect was that this caller never said which of the two cases it is. So the gate is not widened: an object a code package really ships still resolves to `'override-artifact'` and is still refused with `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`.

## Tests — extended in place, not written in parallel

All five new cases live in the #6215 pin suite (`packages/objectql/src/protocol-commit-history.test.ts`), driving `revertCommit` against the real repository over that file's package-aware engine double. Its header comment — which named this issue as the reason its own fixture had to use `view` — is updated rather than left pointing at an open defect.

- a package-bound runtime-created `object` reverts: `revertedCount: 1`, `failed: []`, pre-commit body back, one row still bound to its package;
- a package-less object reverts identically;
- an artifact-backed object is **still refused**: `code: 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'` plus the condition's own first sentence, and the commit's edit is still the live body. Envelope note (ADR-0112): `revertCommit`'s `failed[]` has a declared shape of `{ type, name, error, code? }` and carries no `status`, so `code` is asserted here and the full `code` + `status` pair is asserted at the throwing surface in `protocol-writepath-object-ownership.test.ts` — the same split #6574's pins used;
- **per item, not per call**: one commit, two objects, opposite verdicts — a hoisted batch intent would have to pick one and be wrong about the other;
- `rollbackToPackageCommit` inheritance, driven over the same loop.

That last one is the case whose assertion had to be chosen carefully: a per-item refusal never throws, so the rollback already recorded the commit as reverted and already answered `success: true` while the object was untouched. Asserting `success` there would have been green on the defect, so the assertion is the **stored body**.

## Reverse verification (direction predicted before running)

Prediction: restoring the no-intent call turns the new object cases red with the issue's own message, while #6574's `view` cases and the artifact-backed refusal stay green. Measured, with the fix hunk reverted and `metadata-protocol` rebuilt:

```
 ❯ src/protocol-commit-history.test.ts (17 tests | 4 failed)
   × a package-bound object reverts: revertedCount 1, failed [], pre-commit body back
   × a package-LESS object reverts identically — the binding was never the cause
   × derives the intent PER ITEM: one object restored, its artifact-backed neighbour refused
   × rolls an object edit back through the loop — and the stored body really moved
 Tests  4 failed | 13 passed (17)
```

The first three failed on `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (`expected [ { type: 'object', ... } ] to deeply equal []`); the rollback case failed on the stored body (`expected [ 'name', 'amount', 'due_date' ] to not include 'due_date'`) exactly as designed. The artifact-backed refusal stayed green, which is the half that proves the derivation states the case instead of widening the gate.

## Two neighbours deliberately NOT fixed here, both filed with their measurement

Each is a different cause on a different line, outside this issue's ruled file surface:

- **#6620** — the soft-remove limb states the same intent as a **constant** (`intent: 'override-artifact'`), so a commit that *created* an object still cannot be reverted. Re-measured on this branch: byte-identical to `main`, fixing the restore limb does not touch it.
- **#6621** — neither limb refreshes the `SchemaRegistry` the way `rollbackMetaItem` does (the #4521 rule). After a successful revert the stored row is `["name","amount"]` while `registry.getObject(...)` still serves `["name","amount","due_date"]`. This is type-agnostic and pre-dates this PR — every overlay-allowed type could already reach that limb — but `object` is where it bites, so the pins here assert the **persisted** row and are explicit about not asserting the registry.

Both are referenced from the code comment on the changed limb so the next reader is not left to re-derive them.

## Gates

Every `check:*` step enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` was run one by one (37 root-scoped + 12 spec-scoped + `check:doc-formula-expressions`): all green. `pnpm lint` green (needs `--max-old-space-size=8192`; the full-repo run OOMs at 4096 in this container). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` green — `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` has no `typecheck` script (it carries a ledger entry; `check:type-check-coverage` is green), and its `tsup` DTS build type-checks the change. Package suites: objectql 148 files / 2500 tests passed, metadata-protocol 58 files / 618 tests passed.
